With the trained constraint values $(s_B,\Delta_{\max},\lambda_{\max},X_{\max})=(1,0.5,1,1)$, $\rho_{\min}=0.607$ and $c=0.5$, the worst-case bound \eqref{eq:lstar} certifies $\ell^\star\in[0.1,0.1]$ (median $0.1$) over the observed pre-trigger norms $\norm{\h_{t_0}}_2$ (median $0.11$) at $\alpha_{\min}=0.5$; the data-dependent refinement that replaces $(\rho_{\min},c)$ by the observed $\sigmamin(\Abar_t)$ and $\norm{\Bbar_t\x_t}_2$ along the trigger gives $\ell^\star$ with $5$th percentile $0.4$ and median $0.5$. The shaded region of \cref{fig:hispa} is drawn at the worst-case integer $\ell^\star=0$. Certifying $\ell^\star\ge24$ at $\alpha_{\min}=0.5$ would require $\Delta_{\max}\lambda_{\max}\le0.029$ (currently $0.500$).

\paragraph{Adaptive attack.} Following \citet{athalye2018obfuscated,carlini2019evaluating} we also optimise the trigger directly against the clamp: a white-box adversary with gradient access through \eqref{eq:clamp} maximises the mean step over the trigger and minimises the post-trigger state norm (GCG-style objective on $\Delta_t$; continuous and token-level variants), and two further objectives target state \emph{content} (maximise $\norm{\h-\h^{\mathrm{clean}}}$ at fixed norm) and the classification margin. At $\ell=24$ the saturating adversary pins $\Delta_t$ to $88\%$ of $\Delta_{\max}$ and reduces the retention ratio to $0.14$ (Theorem~\ref{thm:retention} lower bound holds), the content adversary moves the state by $1.18$ relative units while keeping its norm, and the margin adversary flips $100\%$ of predictions; the published Z-/M-HiSPA triggers reach $\alpha=1.98$/$0.52$.
